_comment: Human QA patch for hyptest.pdf, applied by tools/kb/chunk.py after the provenance
re-sort and before segmentation. Every edit a human made to docling's output lives
here, never in the generated chunks — so the build stays reproducible and each
Matching is CONTENT-ADDRESSED (match_prefix on normalised text), not index-based, so
the patch survives a docling re-run that renumbers items. chunk.py fails loudly if a
patch entry matches zero items or more than one.

ops.why: docling classified the standalone beta as a page footer. Dropping page_footer items would silently delete the Type II error rate — the one symbol the section exists to define.
Stray combining not-equal glyph left over from typesetting H1: mu_X != mu_Y. The inequality is already correct inside the adjacent formula item.
Missing word space in docling's output.
ops.set_text: A small p-value indicates that the observed result would be unlikely under the null hypothesis.

ops.why: CodeFormula emitted 'Type I error' as separate letters, which tokenises badly and reads as noise. Semantics unchanged.
ops.match_prefix: P ( T y p e I e r r o r )

ops.why: Third instance of the CodeFormula digit-spacing artefact: 'k = 1 0 \, 0 0 0' does not read as ten thousand. Found by the gold-set eval — q09 ('how many times should I shuffle the labels?') retrieved the Permutation Tests intro instead of the Algorithm chunk that actually states the count.
Mangled Unicode for mu-hat. These are the sample-mean estimators students search for by name.
ops.match_prefix: where ˆ µ X and ˆ µ Y
ops.set_text: where $\hat{\mu}_X$ and $\hat{\mu}_Y$ denote the sample means.

ops.why: Chi-square is a searchable term; 'χ 2 -test' does not match a query for 'chi-squared test'.

TableFormer collapsed the 2x2 decision table into a single data row: 'H 0 true H 0 false' | 'Correct Type II error' | 'Type I error Correct'. All four outcomes are present but the row mapping is destroyed, which would let the tutor state confidently that a Type I error occurs when H0 is false. Replaced with the source table.
ops.markdown:
|              | Accept $H_0$   | Reject $H_0$   |
| ------------ | -------------- | -------------- |
| $H_0$ true   | Correct        | Type I error   |
| $H_0$ false  | Type II error  | Correct        |

heading_hierarchy._comment: docling emitted every section_header at level=1, so hierarchy must be derived. Numbered headings are top level; unnumbered ones nest under the most recent numbered heading.
